outcome: One controller now owns applying code edits; Apply is a real command; two Metrics-marker defects fixed
owner_impact: Applying edits now has a single owner. Before, the editor code (configuration, initialization, controller) and the Metrics code both wrote the status line and the Apply button, and the Metrics code applied Metrics-only edits by catching the Apply click before anyone else. Now one authoring controller decides; the simulator and the Metrics code report to it, and Apply is a direct command. Two existing defects are fixed. (1) If you edited Metrics and the controller and the controller had an error, the Metrics tab lost its 'unapplied' marker although nothing was applied; it now keeps it. (2) When an Experiment load applied the configuration, it also applied your Metrics edits, but the Metrics tab kept saying 'unapplied'; it is now cleared. Everything else behaves exactly as before: on the complete page, all other steps of 28 apply scenarios (Metrics only, while running, Metrics errors, invalid configuration, Metrics with configuration or controller, double Apply, applies started by the Experiment loader) matched production, as did the earlier editor, simulation and results checks. Test now: yes, a short check. Edit only Metrics and Apply; edit Metrics and the controller and Apply; put an error in the controller while Metrics is also edited, press Apply, and check that both tabs still show unapplied edits.

next.text: Next is #569, the last stage of the plan: stop building the hidden duplicate old views and replace the whole-page watchers that fire on every page change, one panel at a time. Nothing changes on screen.

technical_evidence: New web/src/authoring-panel/authoring-machine.js (pure apply rules) and authoring-controller.js (wiring, loaded early by metrics-runtime-bridge.js so it works even if later modules fail). Metrics-only edits go to the metrics participant; otherwise setup, else controller. A setup/controller apply requested through Apply or by another module clears pending Metrics on success and leaves every edit pending on failure.

main.js reports setup/controller outcomes (sourceStatus) and requests (sourceApplyRequest) in the runtime model and exposes applySetup/applyController as simulation commands; the legacy #apply-setup/#compile buttons call them. controls.applySources replaces reading their disabled state.
metrics-runtime-bridge.js no longer intercepts the Apply click, watches feedback text or writes the status; it reports edits, success and failure. authoring-workspace.js keeps only tab plumbing.

Full-page A/B (production versus this build, mirrored libraries): 28 extended apply scenarios identical except the 6 steps showing the two intended fixes; editor 16/16, simulation 18/18, results 11/11 identical; baseline repeatability checked (production versus production identical). A planted rule change is detected.
New web/tests/authoring-machine.test.mjs: 10 behaviour tests including both fixes; planted rule changes are each caught. 683 tests pass. Style comparison identical at all four viewports.
